newsitem.title: USA: Chicago eyes conduit financing for Catholic school.
newsitem.headline: Chicago eyes conduit financing for Catholic school.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley has proposed the city's first conduit financing for a Catholic high school.

The $7 million, letter of credit-backed variable-rate note issue would be sold through the city for De La Salle High School on the city's south side, according to Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer.
The introduction of the proposal at last Friday's city council meeting reportedly prompted questions by several alderman about separation of church and state matters.
But Knorr and the sole manager for the deal said those questions have already been answered by bond attorneys working on the deal who found no problem with the city acting as a conduit issuer.

Knorr said the tax-exempt deal would be similar to the city's role as a conduit issuer for industrial development bonds. This time the deal would be sold for a 501(c)3 Catholic school, the first deal of its kind for the city, he added.
He said the city would not be lending any financial or administrative support to the issue, which would be backed by a letter of credit from Northern Trust Bank.
"All we are doing is giving (the high school) access to the market," Knorr said.

Anthony Fratto, a senior vice president and manager in the Chicago office of George K. Baum & Co, the deal's sole manager, said other religious schools have done similar financings through Illinois Development Finance Authority.
Fratto said proceeds from the De La Salle issue would be used to build a sports center and for other improvements. The school plans to uses pledges and grants to pay off the debt, he added.
Knorr said a hearing on the proposal should be held later this month. If the deal is approved by the City Council Finance Committee, he said it could go before the full council at its Feb 28 meeting.
